method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.reason: Geopolitical escalation (Middle East tensions) is a clear risk-off trigger for Asian equities via higher oil/inflation risk and flow volatility. Regional market-opening headline is directly equity-relevant; assigned high directional negativity and moderate relevance as it reflects immediate market s

Equities.title: Equities: Chip slump and oil surge weigh – Deutsche Bank
Equities.summary: Deutsche Bank strategists report that US equities, particularly tech and semiconductor names, sold off as Oil prices spiked and AI-related sentiment softened.
Equities.reason: Captures two dominant equity impulses today: a renewed oil-driven risk premium and a cooling AI/semiconductor trade. Sector-driven tech weakness combined with macro shock increases market downside risk — elevated directional negative and above-average relevance for cross-market transmission.

Equities.title: US Stocks Fall as Iran Blockade Restarts; Oil Surges Above $80
Equities.reason: Major US market-level headline tying geopolitical escalation to broad equity futures weakness and a material oil move. High directional negative and elevated relevance because it signals a market-regime swing (risk-off, higher inflation expectations) that impacts broad indices and rates/liquidity.

Equities.title: Wall Street ends lower as Iran tensions dampen risk appetite; chipmakers drop
Equities.reason: Reinforces the prevailing risk-off theme: Iran tensions are denting risk appetite and amplifying the semiconductor pullback. Important because it confirms market-close outcomes and sector leadership changes, so given substantial relevance to overall equity sentiment.

Equities.title: SK Hynix Shares Waver in Seoul After Wall Street AI Memory Rout
Equities.reason: Representative semiconductor/AI leadership story showing the sector-specific re-pricing that is leading broader tech weakness. Relevant as a sector-lead indicator for global equity tech exposure; treated as industry-level rather than isolated single-stock noise.

Equities.title: China's exports ride AI boom as domestic economy struggles
Equities.reason: Positive for tech/AI-exposed exporters and EM equity flows — supports the underlying AI leadership narrative even as domestic demand shows weakness. Assigned modest positive direction and relevance as it offsets some of the downside tech/geo headlines but is more structural and regionally focused.

Equities.title: Taiwan's second-largest chipmaker starts mass production in Singapore; Citi sees improving outlook
Equities.summary: Taiwan’s UMC has kicked off mass production of silicon photonics wafers at its Singapore facility amid positive Citi forecast.
Equities.reason: Firm-level/sector-positive development for semiconductors and photonics supply chain that could support earnings visibility for parts of the chip value chain. Useful signal but lower relevance because it's company-specific rather than a market-wide driver.

Equities.title: Big banks poised to report booming revenue propelled by SpaceX IPO, Iran war volatility
Equities.summary: Big banks are set to report booming Q2 revenue as the SpaceX IPO, Iran war volatility and a rebound in commercial lending fuel Wall Street's "sweet spot."
Equities.reason: Banks can be beneficiaries of IPO activity and volatility-driven trading revenues; this is a positive, targeted sector offset to the broader risk-off narrative. Moderate relevance since financials are a large market component but the effect is earnings/flow-specific.

Equities.title: Global investors turn most bullish since February, BofA survey shows
Equities.reason: Sentiment survey indicating improved investor risk appetite — a contrarian/offsetting datapoint to the day's geopolitical and tech weakness. Given survey nature and timing, relevance is modest compared with immediate market-moving headlines.

Rates.title: US Dollar: Fed reaction focus after Waller – MUFG
Rates.summary: MUFG’s Michael Wan notes the Dollar strengthened as US Treasury yields rose and equities sold off, helped by renewed US–Iran tensions and higher Oil prices.
Rates.reason: Explicit note that US Treasury yields rose (driven by geopolitical risk and oil) — direct negative for bond prices / rates (higher-for-longer narrative).

Rates.title: Oil hits $86 as battle for Strait of Hormuz alarms energy markets
Rates.summary: Stocks and bonds hit by higher oil price as fears rise over renewed inflation shock
Rates.reason: Clear transmission: rising oil on Middle East hostilities lifts inflation fears and has already hit bonds — strong negative signal for rates (selloff / hike odds rising).

Rates.title: Waller says Fed shouldn't 'fight the last war' on inflation but warns hikes still possible
Rates.summary: The Fed governor said inflation has expanded beyond the often-cited drivers such as the energy price spike in tariffs.
Rates.reason: Fed official signalling hikes still possible and shifting inflation drivers implies a hawkish stance and higher bond yields — negative for rates.

Rates.title: US CPI data set to show inflation cooled in June due to tumbling fuel prices

Rates.reason: Expected cooler CPI (driven by lower fuel) would relieve inflation pressures and be positive for bonds (yields down) — included as a counter-signal with moderate relevance.

Rates.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Consolidates gains above 0.8130 with US CPI, Fed Warsh in focus
Rates.summary: The US Dollar (USD) is trading practically flat against the Swiss Franc (CHF) on Tuesday, consolidating gains after a 0.7% rally on Monday, boosted by rising geopolitical tensions and hawkish Comments by Federal Reserve (Fed) Governor Christopher Waller.
Rates.reason: Links hawkish Fed commentary and geopolitical tensions to recent USD/risk moves — implies higher US yields and bond weakness; moderate relevance for rates.

Rates.title: A July rate hike from the Fed? The odds are rising
Rates.summary: Chances of a rate hike in July by the Federal Reserve rose as oil prices jumped on the latest developments in the Strait of Hormuz.
Rates.reason: Market odds of a near-term Fed hike increasing (linked to oil shock) — direct negative for bond prices / rates narrative (higher-for-longer).

Rates.title: Indian Rupee slumps amid dual pressure from higher oil prices, Treasury yields
Rates.summary: The Indian Rupee trades significantly lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The USD/INR pair posts a fresh seven-week high near 96.13 as surging oil prices and United States (US) Treasury Yields due to threats of levy from Washington have weakened the
Rates.reason: Shows EM FX/asset spillover from higher oil and rising US Treasury yields — supports broader narrative of higher global yields and tighter financial conditions.

Rates.title: Japan’s bond market is back in play after decades in the wilderness
Rates.summary: JGBs have been selling off amid policy normalization and concerns over Tokyo's spending plans, but experts say that they deserve another look from investors.
Rates.reason: JGB selloff signals global rates repricing and policy normalization pressures — relevant to global bond-market supply/yield dynamics (negative for bond prices).

Rates.title: Fed Rate-Hike Bets Mount Before Inflation Data, Warsh Testimony
Rates.reason: Title indicates markets are upping Fed-hike probability ahead of CPI and Fed testimony — direct negative for bond prices / yields as hike bets rise.

FX.title: Australian Dollar treads water above 0.6900, amid the risk-off market mood
FX.summary: The Australian Dollar (AUD) posts moderate gains against the US Dollar on Tuesday, bouncing to the 0.6930 area from session lows near 0.6910.
FX.reason: Idiosyncratic short-term AUD bounce versus USD in a risk-off backdrop. Positive for AUDUSD but limited market-moving weight; relevance is modest as it's a single-session move without a clear macro catalyst beyond general risk tone.

FX.title: Euro declines against Canadian Dollar as oil prices rise
FX.summary: EUR/CAD extends its losing streak for the third consecutive day, trading around 1.6070 during the European hours on Tuesday. The currency cross depreciates as the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) gains ground on higher oil prices.
FX.reason: Clear commodity-FX transmission: rising oil is strengthening CAD versus EUR (and versus USD by extension). Commodity-driven CAD moves are high-relevance for FX desks given liquidity and correlation with oil — this reinforces a CAD-strength narrative.

FX.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Surging Oil prices back further downside
FX.summary: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades higher against its major currency peers, except antipodeans, during the European trading session on Tuesday.
FX.reason: Explicit FX forecast linking surging oil to further CAD appreciation (USD/CAD lower). High relevance because oil-driven moves in CAD are a direct and market-relevant transmission channel impacting USD-denominated pairs and hedging flows.

FX.title: Australian Dollar: Waiting for Australian data before RBA – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Volkmar Baur at Commerzbank notes the Australian Dollar (AUD) has traded largely sideways, with markets waiting for clarity on Middle East developments and upcoming Australian labor and inflation data ahead of the August 11 Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) meet
FX.reason: Market is in a holding pattern awaiting local data and RBA guidance; this is a low-signal but relevant short-term datapoint for AUD positioning. Assigned low directionality and modest relevance.

FX.title: US Dollar Index: DXY could reach 102 as Gulf tensions persist - ING
FX.summary: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note that higher Crude and Gulf tensions are not yet fully priced, leaving short-term upside risks for the US Dollar (USD).
FX.reason: Stronger DXY call tied to Gulf tensions and oil is a high-relevance USD-support narrative. Significant because a rising DXY alters cross flows and risk-premia across major FX pairs; scored strongly negative for non-USD pairs in line with USD-centric framework.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Stays weak within broad band against US Dollar – UOB
FX.summary: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report USD/JPY rebounded from 161.26 to trade between 161.55 and 162.48, closing firm at 162.42. They see scope for a test of 162.70 while keeping 163.00 out of view, with support at 162.20/162.00.
FX.reason: USD/JPY trading around multi-year weak JPY levels — a clear USD-strength / JPY-weakness signal. JPY moves at these levels have cross-asset and intervention implications, so relevance is above average; direction is negative for JPY (i.e., JPY weakness).

FX.title: ECB selects 36 payment service providers to join digital euro pilot
FX.reason: ECB's digital euro pilot is a central-bank driven initiative with potential structural implications for euro liquidity/usefulness. Immediate FX impact is limited, so scored small positive for EUR (longer-term potential to support EUR liquidity and internationalisation).

FX.title: New Zealand Dollar holds gains near 0.5800, unfazed by risk aversion
FX.summary: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) appreciates against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, hardly affected by the risk-averse scenario.
FX.reason: NZD resilience amid risk-off is a detectable cross-currency flow signal (NZDUSD strength). Relevant for positioning in antipodeans, but not a dominant macro driver — moderate relevance and positive direction for NZD.

FX.title: British Pound flat below 217.00 as JPY intervention risks cap gains; bullish bias intact
FX.summary: The GBP/JPY cross struggles to gain any meaningful traction and seesaws between tepid gains/minor losses through the early part of the European session on Tuesday.
FX.reason: Article flags JPY intervention risk — a high-impact FX event. Intervention risk tends to limit JPY weakness (support JPY), which is material for global FX positioning and crosses. High relevance because intervention talk can re-shape flows and risk premia.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Asset flows and valuation support – DBS
FX.summary: DBS Group Research economist Chang Wei Liang analyses long-term Japanese Yen valuation using DBS’s DEER framework, highlighting that JPY remains significantly undervalued near historically weak levels.
FX.reason: Longer-term valuation/asset-flow analysis argues for JPY support from undervaluation. Not an immediate trade signal but adds to the broader theme that JPY weakness may be mean-reverting; moderate relevance and positive for JPY.

FX.title: South Korea Plans FX Rule Easing to Expand Won’s Global Use
FX.reason: Regulatory/FX rule changes to expand the won's global use are explicitly FX-policy moves. These can increase convertibility and longer-term demand for KRW — medium-high relevance for FX markets given direct policy transmission to flows and liquidity.

Commodities.title: Trump's Hormuz toll plans bring oil supply risks back in spotlight
Commodities.summary: While the proposed levy would raise shipping costs, an escalating conflict could remove barrels from the market altogether.
Commodities.reason: Policy proposal to levy transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz raises shipping costs and the risk of barrels being sidelined — meaningful upward pressure on oil risk premium.

Commodities.reason: Major wire report of oil reaching multi-week highs amid escalation in the Gulf — broad market-moving confirmation of tighter supply/backstop fears.

Commodities.title: Asian Oil Buyers Look to US Crude Again as Iran War Intensifies
Commodities.reason: Demand and trade-flow shift toward US crude as Gulf supplies become riskier — supportive for US crude and pricing differential dynamics, but secondary to outright supply disruption.

Commodities.summary: U.S. petroleum exports reached a record in April as disruptions to international crude oil and refined product flows through the Strait of Hormuz increased global demand for U.S. exports. Exports increased to 13.6 million barrels per day (b/d) in April, 15% mo
Commodities.reason: Record US exports enhance global supply flexibility and can offset some Gulf-related tightness — modestly negative for the pure supply-shock oil narrative.

Commodities.title: The United States produced more crude oil than any other country in 2025
Commodities.summary: The United States remained the world's largest crude oil producer in 2025, according to our International Energy Statistics database, extending a streak that began in 2018 when the United States overtook Russia to become the world's leading producer.
Commodities.reason: U.S. production dominance is a structural dampener on extreme price spikes by increasing available global supply — relevant but lower immediacy than Gulf disruptions.

Commodities.title: Gold: Oil spike weighs on prices – OCBC

Commodities.title: Gold sticks to gains above $4,000; lacks bullish conviction ahead of US CPI, Fed's Warsh

Commodities.reason: Gold showing limited conviction ahead of CPI and Fed commentary; minor short-term downside bias but lower immediate market impact than oil headlines.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD trades higher around $58 in countdown to US CPI data
Commodities.summary: Silver price (XAG/USD) is up 0.75% to near $58 during the European trading session on Tuesday.
Commodities.reason: Modest intraday silver upside ahead of CPI; low-relevance short-term price move consistent with precious metals volatility around macro data.
